sources.entry: Crisp - Menu bar app for external displays: HiDPI scaling, DDC brightness and volume, presets and virtual displays.

summary.one_liner: Crisp is a free, open-source native macOS menu bar app for controlling external monitors, offering HiDPI scaling, DDC brightness and volume, presets, display arrangement, and virtual displays.
summary.what_it_does: Crisp adds display controls that macOS lacks: HiDPI resolutions on external monitors so text is sharp, set up automatically for 1440p and larger at the panel's full refresh rate. It controls monitor backlight brightness and speaker volume over DDC, with software dimming as a fallback, and can route keyboard brightness keys to other displays. Users can save presets (resolution, brightness, arrangement, image adjustment, HDR, enabled displays) and apply them from the menu, Shortcuts, or the crispctl command line tool. It also offers a drag-to-arrange display canvas, disconnecting and reconnecting displays, input switching over DDC, system toggles like Dark Mode and Night Shift, ICC profile and image adjustment controls, and virtual HiDPI displays. The README says the app is available in English, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese.
use_cases: fix blurry text on an external monitor
control external monitor brightness from the Mac
adjust monitor speaker volume over DDC
save and switch display layouts with presets
automate day and night display setups with Shortcuts
switch a monitor between computer inputs
how_to_run: Or download Crisp.dmg from the releases and drag Crisp to Applications
notable: Free with no Pro tier or license key, positioned as an alternative to BetterDisplay and Lunar
crispctl command line tool and an AI agent skill for Claude Code and Codex
Extra Brightness pushes XDR and HDR panels past 100%
Managed Mac configuration profile can disable Keep Awake
Forked from FreeDisplay and substantially rewritten
caveats: Smooth scaling needs a one-time administrator password per monitor to install a protected display override file
Brightness Keys need Accessibility permission; Extra Brightness draws more power and HDR video can look overblown while on
crispctl requires the Crisp app to be running
